title: Stack with popMin and popMax
statement:
Design a special stack of integers that behaves like an ordinary stack but additionally lets you remove its smallest or its largest element.

The stack supports these operations:

- `push x`: put `x` on top of the stack. Prints nothing.
- `pop`: remove the top element and print it.
- `top`: print the top element without removing it.
- `popMin`: remove the **smallest** element in the stack and print it. If the smallest value occurs several times, remove the one closest to the top (the most recently pushed).
- `popMax`: remove the **largest** element in the stack and print it. If the largest value occurs several times, remove the one closest to the top (the most recently pushed).

After `popMin` or `popMax`, the remaining elements keep their relative stack order. You are given a sequence of operations; print one line for each operation other than `push`. The sequence is guaranteed to contain at least one operation other than `push`, and the stack is never empty when `pop`, `top`, `popMin` or `popMax` is called.

**Follow-up:** The interviewer asked for `popMin` and `popMax` in `O(1)`, with the hint to keep one auxiliary stack for the minimum and one for the maximum. Think about why this cannot hold for arbitrary operation sequences: if `popMin` were `O(1)`, repeated `popMin` calls would sort `n` numbers in `O(n)` comparisons. The achievable bound is `O(log n)` per operation, which is what the tests here require.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `q`, the number of operations.
Each of the next `q` lines is one operation: `push x`, `pop`, `top`, `popMin` or `popMax`.
outputFormat: For every operation other than `push`, print the value it returns on its own line, in order.
constraints: The stack is non-empty whenever pop, top, popMin or popMax is called
At least one operation is not a push

hints: A plain stack handles push, pop and top. The hard part is that popMin and popMax delete from the middle of the stack, so give every pushed element a unique id.
Keep a min-heap ordered by (value, -id) and a max-heap ordered by (-value, -id), so that ties resolve to the most recently pushed element.
Delete lazily: mark an id as removed when any operation removes it, and discard removed ids when they surface at the top of the stack or of either heap.
